If a lead with this email exists (the newest one, leaving out leads already converted to a contact), it is returned unchanged, and gets a note when the 'Note for an existing lead' fields are filled in. If none exists, a lead is created from the fields here. Made for web forms: it takes a full name from one box and doesn't need a company. The result says which happened (created, and outcome in plain words) and gives the lead's ID, name, company, owner and a link to open it, the same fields either way.

parameters.description: Beta. Only run for leads with this Lead Source, written as it appears in Salesforce, such as Web. Leave blank to run for every new lead.

salesforce_new_opportunity_trigger.description: Runs for each new opportunity (deal) in Salesforce, or only for those worth at least an amount you choose. It arrives with its owner's name and email, its account's name and a link to it. Opportunities already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.AccountId: The record ID of its account.
output.CloseDate: When it is expected to close.
output.IsClosed: Whether it is closed, won or lost.
output.Name: The opportunity's name.
output.Probability: How likely it is to close, in percent.
output.StageName: The stage it is in, such as Prospecting.
output.Type: Its type, such as New Customer.
output.account_name: Beta. The name of its account (the customer); blank when it has none.
output.amount_display: Beta. Its value as a person writes it, such as 62,500. Use it in a message, with your currency sign in front; compare with Amount.
output.custom_fields: Beta. The fields named in Extra fields, each by its API name, such as custom_fields.Discount_Percent__c. Empty when none were asked for.
output.opportunity_link: Beta. A link that opens the opportunity in Salesforce.
output.owner_email: Beta. Their email address, ready to send them a message.
output.owner_first_name: Beta. The owner's first name, such as Dana, to greet them by in a message.
output.owner_name: Beta. The name of the person who owns the opportunity, usually its sales rep.

parameters.description: Beta. Only run for opportunities worth this much or more, as a plain number such as 50000. An opportunity with no amount doesn't run it. Leave blank to run whatever the amount.
parameters.name: min_amount

parameters.description: Beta. Your org's own fields to read as well, by their API names with commas between them, such as Discount_Percent__c, Region__c. Each arrives under custom_fields, such as custom_fields.Discount_Percent__c. A field's API name is shown in Salesforce under Setup > Object Manager > Opportunity > Fields & Relationships. Leave blank for none.
parameters.name: extra_fields

salesforce_new_record_trigger.description: Runs for each new record of the object you choose, such as an account, a case or one of your org's own objects, with its fields by their API names. Records already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.Name: Its name, for an object that has one.
output.OwnerId: The record ID of its owner, for an object that has one.

parameters.description: What kind of record to watch, such as Account, Case or one of your org's own objects.
parameters.name: object_type

salesforce_opportunity_stage_changed_tri.description: Runs when an opportunity moves to a new stage in Salesforce, or only when it moves to the stage you choose, such as Closed Won, or is worth at least an amount you choose. It arrives with its owner's name and email, its account's name and a link to it, so no further step is needed to look them up. A deal that moves on and back again runs it again. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.AccountId: The record ID of its account.
output.CloseDate: When it is expected to close.
output.IsClosed: Whether it is closed, won or lost.
output.Name: The opportunity's name.
output.Probability: How likely it is to close, in percent.
output.StageName: The stage it is in, such as Prospecting.
output.Type: Its type, such as New Customer.
output.account_name: Beta. The name of its account (the customer); blank when it has none.
output.amount_display: Beta. Its value as a person writes it, such as 62,500. Use it in a message, with your currency sign in front; compare with Amount.
output.custom_fields: Beta. The fields named in Extra fields, each by its API name, such as custom_fields.Discount_Percent__c. Empty when none were asked for.
output.opportunity_link: Beta. A link that opens the opportunity in Salesforce.
output.owner_email: Beta. Their email address, ready to send them a message.
output.owner_first_name: Beta. The owner's first name, such as Dana, to greet them by in a message.
output.owner_name: Beta. The name of the person who owns the opportunity, usually its sales rep.

parameters.description: Only run when an opportunity moves to this stage, written as it appears in Salesforce, such as Closed Won. Leave blank to run for every move. Capitals don't matter, but the name must be the whole of one of your org's stages: turning the workflow on is refused, listing them, when it isn't. Salesforce's standard stages are Prospecting, Qualification, Needs Analysis, Value Proposition, Id. Decision Makers, Perception Analysis, Proposal/Price Quote, Negotiation/Review, Closed Won and Closed Lost.
parameters.name: stage_name

salesforce_updated_record_trigger.description: Runs each time a record of the object you choose is changed in Salesforce, such as an account, a case or one of your org's own objects, with its fields as they are now. A new record doesn't run it until it is changed. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.Name: Its name, for an object that has one.
output.OwnerId: The record ID of its owner, for an object that has one.
